roundDelta: The whole round is one forward merge of main, made because GitHub reported the head CONFLICTING and ran no check on it. sjawhar/legion#2528 (dispatch://INFRA-774, clusterOnly) merged at 9d60d92f and conflicted in packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch.go, gcp/dispatch_kube.go and infra/README.md. Every resolution keeps both sides, as the two implementers agreed before either pushed. The merge also carries one change of its own, which the clean merge made necessary: #2528's TestDispatchEveryInputIsLiveOrRefusedUnderClusterOnly holds dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals complete against DispatchArgs, and this branch's three inputs were in neither, so the merged tree failed that test until each was added as a refusal row. This round writes .legion/INFRA-550/ again, which retro removed; the next retro removes it again.

proof.criterion: The branch builds and its own tests hold at the merge head — the check a forward merge owes, since a clean merge can still change behaviour under the branch's callers.
proof.surface: The Go module packages/envoy/infra at the merge commit, the repository's own envoy-infra-go lane.
proof.command: cd packages/envoy/infra && test -z "$(gofmt -l .)"; go vet -tags pulumilive,natslive ./...; go test ./... -skip 'TestTheDataDiskIsFormattedOnlyWhenItReadsAsZerosToItsEnd|TestARefusedDataDiskIsNeverFormattedOnALaterBoot' -count=1
proof.observed: gofmt empty, vet clean, and every package ok, gcp included (128.0 s). The merge did change behaviour before the fix: at the resolved tree, before the refusal rows were added, TestDispatchEveryInputIsLiveOrRefusedUnderClusterOnly failed with 53 inputs against 50 covered, naming natsInCluster, natsReplicas and streamMaxBytes. Adding the three rows to dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals (gcp/dispatch.go) and to its test table (gcp/dispatch_cluster_only_test.go) is the whole of this round's own change.
proof.negativeControl: The failing run is the control: the same command at the same tree without the three rows fails that one test and names the three missing inputs, so the suite is what holds the census complete rather than a comment. The two tests skipped need mkfs.ext4, which this container has not got; CI runs them.
proof.note: go test -tags natslive ./core/ ./seed/ ./gcp/ needs Docker, which this container has not got: CI owns that lane.

proof.criterion: A consumer can still pass the three inputs after the merge, on the surface agent-infra's dispatch/ program uses — the proof re-run at the merge head, as a forward merge requires.
proof.surface: The built pulumi-resource-envoy-infra driven by the real Pulumi CLI v3.268.0, on a file:// backend under $TMPDIR with PULUMI_HOME set and PULUMI_ACCESS_TOKEN empty from the first call.
proof.command: go build -ldflags '-X main.version=0.0.1' -o $TMPDIR/infra-550/pulumi-resource-envoy-infra ./cmd/pulumi-resource-envoy-infra; pulumi plugin install resource envoy-infra 0.0.1 --file <binary>; pulumi package get-schema <binary>; pulumi package add <binary> in a scratch Go module; go build ./... of a consumer constructing gcp:Dispatch with natsInCluster true, natsReplicas 3, streamMaxBytes 1073741824 and natsUrl nats://envoy-hub.envoy.svc.cluster.local:4222; pulumi preview
proof.observed: The schema still carries natsInCluster {"type":"boolean","plain":true}, natsReplicas and streamMaxBytes as plain integers, beside #2528's clusterOnly, and requiredInputs is now hostname and region alone, since #2528 made thirteen inputs optional. The SDK the CLI generated at this head declares NatsInCluster *bool, NatsReplicas *int and StreamMaxBytes *int; the consumer program needed pulumi.StringRef on seven inputs that are now optional, which is #2528's breaking change and not this branch's. pulumi preview reached 'envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch resource example-dispatch has a problem: envoy-infra:gcp:Dispatch needs a "gcp" provider in its providers option', the providers.Require gate, reached only after the resolver accepted all four inputs.
proof.negativeControl: Two, both through the plugin at this head. natsReplicas: 6 fails earlier, at the resolver: 'natsReplicas 6 is above 5, the most copies NATS keeps'. And the interaction the merge created: a cluster-only program setting region, hostname, clusterOnly and natsInCluster alone is refused 'natsInCluster configures Dispatch, which clusterOnly does not build: unset it, or unset clusterOnly' — the refusal row this round added, driven through the released-plugin surface rather than through the unit test alone.

filesChanged: packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch.go: the dispatchSettings doc comment carries both branches' sentences, and dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals gains natsInCluster, natsReplicas and streamMaxBytes, in DispatchArgs' own order, after listenerReplicas.

packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_kube.go: #2528's removal of the dispatchKubernetes struct and its error-only returns, with this branch's natsInCluster gating of the front door's Service, the DependsOn both workloads carry and the port-1055 ingress rule.

packages/envoy/infra/gcp/dispatch_cluster_only_test.go: the same three rows in dispatchClusterOnlyRefusals' test table, so TestDispatchEveryInputIsLiveOrRefusedUnderClusterOnly holds again and TestDispatchClusterOnlyRefusesEveryDispatchInput drives each refusal.

packages/envoy/infra/README.md: #2528's clusterOnly column, its sentences and its provider paragraph, beside this branch's natsInCluster clauses; the Services row carries both, reading '(two Services with natsInCluster)' in its first cell and 'Not built' in the clusterOnly column.
trickyParts: The merge is a genuine fast-forward of the branch: jj new legion/INFRA-550 main@origin, never a rebase, so nothing already pushed moved and no other tree's work was rewritten.

Keeping both sides was agreed with #2528's implementer over Envoy before either branch pushed, down to the Services row: this branch's parenthesis in its first cell and #2528's third column with 'Not built'. The agreement is what made three conflicts a mechanical resolution.

The only semantic breakage a clean text merge left was the input census. It is exactly the hazard the forward-merge rule names, and it was found by running the suite at the merge head rather than by reading the diff.
deviations: The merge commit carries one change of its own — the three refusal rows and their test rows — rather than a commit above it, because the rows are in the same files and hunks as the resolution and cannot be split by path. The commit message says so.
discoveredComplexity: #2528 made thirteen gcp:Dispatch inputs optional, so a consumer written against the earlier SDK no longer compiles: seven plain strings are now *string. That is #2528's own breaking change, which its title marks, and it reached this branch only as a change to the throwaway consumer program of the proof.
